newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite crude slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite crude slide.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to slightly higher again Wednesday, in moderate activity boosted by forecasts for colder East Coast weather and a record rally in natgas, industry sources said.

"Everyone in New York is getting bullish because of the weather and gas prices, but there still aren't tons of utilities looking to buy oil," said one cash trader, noting cold weather should boost utility burns and eventually trim stocks.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent edged up slightly to $21.75 a barrel on prospects for better utility interest.
NYH December one percent paper climbed above $22.00 early but later was quoted little changed at $21.75 or lower on softer crude, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH held steady, with 2.2 percent still at $20.25-50.
A Midwest utility tendered for 0.7 percent material for December delivery. Bids are due Tuesday, November 26.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $18.75-19.00 and three percent at $17.75-18.00.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York City gate swing gas surged almost 40 cents Wednesday to about $4.00/mmBtu on forecasts for colder weather later this week and next. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.45/mmBtu equivalent. In December, New York gas remained quoted at $1.35 over the NYMEX screen, or near $5.00/mmBtu versus resid paper at a $3.45/mmBtu equivalent.
